The [[Copa del Rey]] is an annual [[Single-elimination tournament|knockout]] [[Association football|football]] competition in [[Spanish football]], organised by the [[Royal Spanish Football Federation]], held annually since [[1903 Copa del Rey|1903]]. The competition is open to all [[La Liga|Primera]] and [[Segunda División]] teams as well as all [[Primera Federación|Primera]], [[Segunda Federación|Segunda]] and [[Tercera División]] sides plus the four semi-finalists of the [[Copa Federación de España|Copa Federación]] and the ten teams from [[Divisiones Regionales de Fútbol|Divisiones Regionales]] after passing a preliminary round. The total, adding up to 116 clubs, excludes Spanish reserve teams.<ref>{{cite web |last=Sanz |first=Javier Domínguez |date=24 May 2026 |title=Los 102 equipos que iniciarán la Copa del Rey 2026–27 |language=es |trans-title=The 102 teams that will play in the 2026–27 Copa del Rey |url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/copa-rey/2026/05/24/102-equipos-iniciaran-copa-rey-2026-27.html |access-date=18 September 2026 |website=Marca}}</ref>

Since the first final between [[Athletic Bilbao]] and [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], 122 single-match finals have taken place. The 1904 final was not held because of a dispute over who should have faced Athletic Bilbao; the latter, having gone to Madrid to play the final nevertheless, were assigned the title.<ref name="copa1904">{{Cite web |date=13 January 2000 |first=José Vicente |last=Tejedor Carnicero |title=Spain – Cups 1904 |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spancup1904.html |access-date=18 September 2026 |website=[[RSSSF]]}}</ref> In [[1910 Copa del Rey|1910]] and [[1913 Copa del Rey|1913]] two parallel tournaments, both eventually recognised, and finals were played due to the conflict between ''Federación Española de Clubs de Football'' (the forerunner of the [[Royal Spanish Football Federation]]) and the ''Unión Española de Clubs de Foot-bal.''<ref name="Martinez2014">{{cite journal |last=Martínez Patón |first=Víctor |date=February 2014 |title=Las siete federaciones españolas de fútbol (IV) |language=Spanish |trans-title=The seven federations of Spanish football |url=https://www.cuadernosdefutbol.com/2014/02/las-siete-federaciones-espanolas-de-futbol-iv/ |journal=Cuadernos de Fútbol |publisher=CIHEFE |issue=54 |access-date=22 September 2026}}</ref> The finals did not take place in 1937 and in 1938 due to the impact of the [[Spanish Civil War]].<ref name=":1" /> The [[2020 Copa del Rey final|2020]] final—due to have taken place in the April of that year between [[Basque derby|Basque clubs]] Athletic Bilbao and [[Real Sociedad]]—was rescheduled to April 2021 in the hope the match could have been played with spectators in the face of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite press release |title=Official Announcement |date=4 May 2020 |url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/2020/05/04/comunicado-oficial-3/ |access-date=18 August 2026 |website=Athletic Bilbao |language=en}}</ref> The match was held [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]] as Real Sociedad won 1–0.<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 April 2021 |title=Una Copa de sobresaliente |language=Spanish |trans-title=An outstanding cup |url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/real-sociedad/2021/04/04/6068682d46163f58048b4605.html |access-date=18 September 2026 |website=Marca |first=Óscar |last=Badallo}}</ref> 

Four finals were replayed after the first games ended in a draw, with 26 others going to extra time and eight of those requiring a penalty shoot-out to decide a winner.<ref name=":1" />

As of 2026, 36 clubs have competed in the final, of whom 15 have won the tournament at least once. The winning team has also won La Liga (the Spanish top-flight league which began in 1929) in the same season on 18 occasions to complete a domestic double. [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] are the only team to win La Liga, the Copa del Rey and the [[UEFA Champions League]] in the same year, having done so twice in 2009 and 2015.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Jeanes |first=Will |date=8 January 2026 |title=Which clubs have won the treble before? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4570948/2023/06/09/past-treble-winners-champions-league-manchester-city/ |access-date=18 September 2026 |work=[[The Athletic]] |url-access=subscription |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> 

Barcelona hold the record for the most wins and most final appearances, with 32 wins from 43 total appearances. Real Madrid hold the record for the most finals lost (21). Of the teams who have participated in more than one final, [[Club Español de Madrid|Español de Madrid]] and [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]] share the worst win–loss record with three defeats and no victories each. Of the victorious teams, [[Arenas Club de Getxo|Arenas]] have the lowest percentage of success, winning one out of four finals (25%). [[Real Sociedad]] are the reigning champions, having won their third title in [[2025–26 Copa del Rey|2026]].<ref name=":1" />

!scope="row"|[[Athletic Bilbao]]{{efn|name=Ath|The number of wins [[Athletic Bilbao]] have been credited with is disputed. The 1902 version was won by Bizcaya, a team made up of players from Athletic Bilbao and Bilbao FC. In 1903 these two clubs merged as the current Athletic Bilbao.
